newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Rubber - Goodyear strike, weak demand to hit prices.
newsitem.headline: Rubber - Goodyear strike, weak demand to hit prices.

text.p: Southeast Asian rubber prices are seen languishing this week on soft demand with the unresolved strike by Goodyear Tire's 13,000 workers making the situation worse, regional dealers said on Monday.
The long Golden Week holidays in Japan and the May day holiday later in the week may also weaken sentiment, they said.
"The Goodyear strike will somehow affect the market. Psychologically, it would impact on sentiment this week," a senior dealer for a rubber trading house in Singapore said.
"If the strike is not solved, the market will become worse and worse," a dealer in Indonesia added.
Traders said a prolonged strike at Goodyear, whose annual consumption of rubber reaches around 300,000 tonnes, will knock prices lower.

"It's already depressing just to think about that," a dealer in the Thai rubber centre of Hat-Yai said, adding the end of wintering and an increase in supplies "will add more pressure to an already bearish market."
Indonesian traders said bids of SIR20 grade rubber were heard at 46.75 U.S. cents a lb FOB Medan for August shipment although no deals were done.

Offer prices were seen at 47.00 cents FOB Medan for June shipment, 46.50 cents a lb FOB Padang, 46.75 cents FOB Surabaya, and at 46.25 cents FOB Jambi. In Pontianak, SIR20 was offered at 46.00 cents FOB.

"Prices continue to fall and this makes traders unwilling to sell. Instead, traders increased their offer prices even though demand is very low, and are hoping that prices will improve soon," a trader said.
Some dealers said SIR20 offer prices could fall to as low as 30.00 U.S. cents a lb because of poor demand.
"We assume that buyers already have enough stock...that's why they don't need to make fresh purchases," said one trader.
"I don't think SIR20 has enough strength to stay at these levels. It's going to drop quite drastically," a Singapore based dealer said.
In Thailand, dealers said recent buying by the Thai government of RSS3 grade rubber at 109.00 U.S. cents a kg did not help the market.

"Their purchases at above average prices drove local prices up and distorted the market. While the local prices were high, bidding prices from foreign buyers were low, reflecting the real market situation. This makes it difficult to sell sometimes," a dealer in Bangkok said.
The Thai benchmark RSS3 grade rubber for July delivery was quoted around 106.00 U.S. cents a kg.
In Malaysia, traders were resigned to seeing prices take another tumble this week with the strike at Goodyear adding a gloomy touch to the market.
"There's nothing on the horizon I see that is going to pull the market out of its present state," a dealer said.

The Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board (MRELB) quoted the benchmark RSS1 at 277.50 Malaysian cents a kg last Friday, down 10 cents from the previous week. The SMR20 for May buyer was quoted seven cents easier at 263.50 cents a kg.
Trading houses were quoting the SMR 20 at around 262 cents a kg, SMR CV at 332 cents, SMR L at 312 cents, SMR 5 at 273 cents, SMR 10 at 260 cents and drum latex at 228 cents.
Traders said supply of latex was increasing and that this was adding to the woes of producers.
-- Singapore Newsroom (65-8703305)
